title: skills.manifest/1
description: The skills manifest: ONE source for every skill and plugin hmd knows about, skills.manifest.json in the repo root. It is to replace heimdall-skills.json (which plugins a project activates), skills-registry.json (GitHub skills matched by keyword) and the auto-install table of skills/heimdall/references/plugin-autoinstall.md with the preinstall code that implements it; while the flag skills.registry is off those three stay authoritative and the manifest only records them, every legacy mapping once, each with a legacy[] pointer to where it came from. THIS FILE AND bin/lib/skills_manifest.py STATE ONE CONTRACT: the validator holds the rules in code and never reads this file at run time (a sandbox that copies bin/lib alone still validates), and test/skills-manifest-schema.test.sh fails when the version, kinds, tiers, patterns or key sets of the two differ. The keywords used here are the subset docs/schemas/runhmd.*.v1.json already uses; JSON Schema cannot express cross-field rules, so `x-invariants` lists the extra rules the validator enforces. WHAT AN ENTRY IS: kind plugin (a Claude Code plugin, ref <plugin>@<marketplace>), github-skill (cloned from GitHub, matched by keywords) or bundled (ships in-tree, never installed). tier says how it is offered: bundled (in-tree), recommended (suggested to a new install, installed only on consent), detected (offered when the project's files or the prompt call for it), on_demand (kept for an explicit request), community (reserved: never auto-suggested). install false marks an activation-only entry that hmd never installs. A marketplace outside the allow-list can therefore appear on an install:false entry and nowhere else. OPTIONAL pack AND on_demand_paths (lean core) belong to bundled entries only: pack describes the in-tree content as a hash-pinned pack (name, version, the full sha256, the tree paths it covers) and on_demand_paths lists the tree paths a lean install leaves out and adds on request; a manifest that uses neither is valid and means what it always meant.

x-invariants.rule: schema is the integer 1: not 1.0, not true, not a string; any other version is a different contract

a plugin entry's ref is <plugin>@<marketplace> with the same marketplace as its marketplace field; when install is true that marketplace is a key of marketplaces, the allow-list: no other marketplace is ever passed to claude
every entry has a non-empty legacy array: no mapping exists without a pointer to the legacy mechanism it came from
triggers.prompt_ere compiles (Python re) and does not match the empty string, which would fire the entry on every prompt; triggers.order values are unique positive integers
a community entry has install false or explicit_consent true
an entry of kind bundled or tier bundled never has install true
a plugin entry has ref and marketplace; a github-skill entry has repo, keywords, category and description; marketplace is null or absent on every other kind
references resolve: detection_rules.*.entries name existing entry ids, activate.detect names existing detection_rules keys, keyword_skills names existing github-skill entries
every path or glob (triggers.files[].path, detection_rules.*.files[], pack.paths[], on_demand_paths[]) is project-relative: no leading slash and no .. segment
free text (why, description, category, keywords, ref, legacy pointers) is non-blank and single-line; the document is strict JSON of at most 1 MiB with no duplicate object keys

pack, when present, has exactly name, version, sha256 and paths: name is @<scope>/<name> (scope and name each match the id pattern), version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -prerelease, sha256 is the full content hash (64 lowercase hex digits: no prefix, no truncation, no upper case) and paths is a non-empty array of install paths

pack and on_demand_paths appear on bundled entries only (in-tree content); on_demand_paths is a non-empty array; every install path in them (pack.paths[], on_demand_paths[]) is one literal tree path: segments of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' joined by '/', each starting with a letter, digit or '_', so no glob, no leading '-', no hidden or '.' segment, no empty segment and no trailing slash

marketplaces.description: The install allow-list: marketplace name -> where it comes from. An install:true plugin entry may only name a marketplace listed here; an activation-only (install:false) entry may name another.

entries.description: Every skill and plugin, one entry each.

detection_rules.description: Verbatim from heimdall-skills.json: rule name -> the project files (globs) that switch its entries on.

keyword_skills.description: Optional: ids of the github-skill entries in the order the legacy registry lists them.

installPath.description: A literal tree path, it ends up in a sparse-checkout command: segments of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' joined by '/', each starting with a letter, digit or '_' (no glob, no leading '-', no hidden or '.' segment, no empty segment, no trailing slash).

sha256.description: The full content hash: 64 lowercase hex digits, no prefix, no truncation.

fileTrigger.description: A project file whose presence triggers the entry; with contains_any, only when the file holds one of the words.

triggers.description: The legacy preinstall rule: prompt_ere is matched unanchored (Python re) against the lower-cased prompt, files are alternatives, order is the position the legacy code emits it in.

activate.description: permanent: always on; detect: the detection_rules that switch it on.

pack.description: The in-tree content of a bundled entry as a pack: name @<scope>/<name>, version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -prerelease, the full sha256 of the pack's content and the tree paths it covers.

why.description: One line, shown wherever the entry is offered or explained.

legacy.description: Where this mapping came from: the legacy mechanism and the place in it. At least one.

ref.description: plugin: <plugin>@<marketplace>; bundled: its in-tree path; github-skill: optional.

marketplace.description: plugin entries only: the marketplace of ref; null or absent on every other kind.

explicit_consent.description: community entries: true lets an install:true entry through, because the operator consents to it explicitly, every time.

repo.description: github-skill entries: the GitHub owner/repo it is cloned from.

keywords.description: github-skill entries: matched as whole words against the prompt.

pack.description: bundled entries only: the in-tree content as a hash-pinned pack.

on_demand_paths.description: bundled entries only: the tree paths a lean install leaves out of the working tree and adds on request.
